terms.meaning: Pictures of the ground taken from space, used here to compare land over time.
The difference between two percentages, such as going from 20 percent to 25 percent is five percentage points.

sections.name: File setup, statusClass
sections.title: Imports and status text helper
sections.what: Brings in the tools and types the panel needs. Also converts a classification value to lowercase so it can be used as a style class name.
sections.why: Keeps the status styling in one small helper that every card uses.
sections.watch_out: The lowercase value is used to build class names, so renaming a classification value will change the styling.

sections.name: ContextImage
sections.title: Drawn before and after pictures
sections.what: Draws one small picture with a label and date, in a green-and-brown style. The picture changes shape depending on whether the area is built up, stable, or changing in a stable way. Each picture is labelled as synthetic.
sections.why: Gives a visual sense of change without using real satellite photos, and the synthetic label keeps it honest.
sections.watch_out: The look is chosen from a visual variant value, so a new variant that is not handled will fall back to the default green look.

sections.name: IndicatorCard
sections.title: Single indicator card
sections.what: Shows one measured theme such as vegetation or built-up area. It gives the status, the earlier and later percentages, the change, and a short explanation.
sections.why: Lets the owner read each change in a simple table-like form.
sections.watch_out: Missing values appear as a dash, so a missing reading can look like no change to someone who skims.

sections.name: EarthObservationContent
sections.title: Full earth observation content
sections.what: Builds the whole results view. It shows a safety note, then either an empty message if evidence is insufficient or the before and after pictures with metadata. Then it lists all indicator cards, an overall summary, and a back link.
sections.why: Puts the full result in a clear order, with the safety note first.
sections.watch_out: The code uses the earlier and later snapshots by position, so a response with fewer than two snapshots could leave those picture slots empty.

sections.name: EarthObservationPanel
sections.title: Loader that fetches the panel data
sections.what: Asks the server for the earth observation result for this case. Shows loading until the data arrives, an error message if the request fails, and otherwise the full content.
sections.why: Keeps the page from freezing while data loads and gives a clear message when it fails.
sections.watch_out: The request is cancelled when the panel leaves the screen, so a fast page change does not show stale results.

sections.name: EarthObservationTeaser
sections.title: Short teaser with link
sections.what: Shows a short heading and description with a button or compact link that opens the full earth observation page.
sections.why: Lets other pages point to the full results without loading them.
sections.watch_out: The link path is built from the case ID, so an incorrect ID would send the user to a page that does not exist.

summary: Shows satellite-style before and after pictures of a parcel with simple change indicators for vegetation, built-up area, surface and water.
purpose: Lets the owner see how the land around the parcel changed over time, with a clear note that the imagery and data are synthetic.
why: Likely reason: the feature shows indicators with a safety note so people do not mistake them for official results. Reason partly stated in the file names and safety text.
how: The full panel loads data from the case earth-observation endpoint and shows a loading message first. Once data arrives, it shows a safety note, either an empty state or two drawn images, a metadata block, one card per indicator, an overall summary and a link back to parcel intelligence. A smaller teaser links to the full page.
inputs: A case ID, the earth-observation API response, and the current language from the locale context.
outputs: A set of images drawn in code, indicator cards with percentages and change values, a summary, and links to other pages.
risks: The indicator and summary text depend on the classification values. A failed request shows an error empty state. The drawn images are illustrative and must not be read as real satellite data.
debug: If the panel stays on loading, check the earth-observation endpoint response. If indicators show dashes, check for missing values in the response. If wording is wrong, check the localized presentation helper.
